_doc: Canonical netflag/netport body-orientation spec. The flag BODY must point
OUTWARD along the stub direction (顺着导线朝外); the wire enters from the
circuit side. This file is the SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH — never hand-edit the
12 numbers in frozenTable; they are DERIVED from rotationCycle + bodyAnchor.
Both consumers derive the same table:
- skills/easyeda-agent/scripts/orient.py  (the linter's check)
- extension/src/actions.ts deriveBodyRotation()  (what connect_pin writes)
tests/run.py asserts derive(cycle, anchors) == frozenTable, so the two
language copies can never drift. calibrate.js re-validates the 3 anchors +
cycle against live getPrimitivesBBox ground truth (run after importing a new
.eext). See docs/schematic-layout-conventions.md §3.5.
2026-06-29 VERTICAL ORIENTATION CALIBRATION (EasyEDA 3.2.149, connector
0.5.21): a flag body's visual up/down mapping differed from the prior cycle
— confirmed by getPrimitivesBBox on REAL, settled, wired flags (a
connect_pin --direction down ground rendered its bars TOWARD the pin; power
--direction up the same). Horizontal (left/right) was unaffected. The old
table slipped through because calibrate.js decoded vertical body direction
incorrectly (fixed there too). The confirmed visual cycle is
up->right->down->left with power/ground anchors swapped so ONLY the up/down
numbers move; every left/right number is byte-identical to before. This
stored-rotation truth is independent of endpoint coordinate signs.

2026-08-12 VERTICAL RE-CALIBRATION (live ceshi board, connector 0.24.3): five rendered ground truths (power up stored=0 [C6 3V3], power right=270 [R2], power left=90 [U2], ground down=0 [C6], ground left=270 [LED1]) contradict the 2026-06-29 table's vertical values (it said power up=180/ground down=180) while matching its horizontal ones. Root cause: the 06-29 fix reversed the CYCLE and compensated with swapped anchors — horizontal happened to line up, vertical stayed inverted, and the linter has been blessing reversed vertical flags ever since (an autoconnect-placed 3V3 stored 180 rendered upside-down and scored clean). The counter-clockwise cycle up->left->down->right with NATURAL anchors (power:up, ground:down, port:right) reproduces ALL five measurements; only up/down numbers move vs 06-29, every left/right number is byte-identical.
